cards.title: Nine classes through expiry and restart
cards.metric_label: 18 teachings, three queries and a process reopen
cards.body: Eight class centroids share one encrypted bank. The complete nine-class lifecycle verifies 2,336 fresh proofs, expires two old examples, and preserves all class sums and exact rankings across restart. Its first query answers eight classes in 87.672 seconds.
cards.limit: A small authored corpus with a surviving full reader. Class availability changes during teaching; this is not a general accuracy benchmark. Native proof and public-transform assumptions remain.

cards.title: A complete learner in the BFV arithmetic fields
cards.body: The exact-field backend removes carry and range witnesses. Twelve teachings, four complete two-class queries, FIFO expiry and restart finish in 638.021 worker seconds, with every returned value matching the reference.
cards.limit: The score and proof profile differ from the quadratic predecessor. No equal-security speedup or numerical soundness level is claimed. Verification still costs more than recomputing this small FHE function; a full reader survives.

cards.title: A corrected complete nonlinear kernel
cards.metric_label: 116 fresh proofs, with arithmetic on every row
cards.body: One saved public class passes a complete fresh consumer after repairing the final-row emitter gap. Compact ranges reduce proof data by 8.19% and MAC proving by 16.85%. All 88 MAC, 4 basis-extension, 18 tensor and 6 rescale proofs are new.
cards.limit: Whole proving improves only 1.69% and peak memory rises. This is one saved class, not a new teaching chain or private-reading run. Native lowering, lookup extraction and the new profile’s full soundness bound remain open; a full reader survives.

cards.title: The earlier fresh teaching integration
cards.metric_label: two teachings, two class answers, four fresh proofs
cards.body: New text updates two encrypted classes. Each update is proved and committed; both class computations are then proved and verified at the accepted model revision before the first private reads. The resulting scores match their integer references.
cards.limit: Historical accepted run: the legacy emitter skipped final-row arithmetic, so these proofs do not establish every intended row. The corrected saved-class successor is separate. The encoder is plaintext and the recipient retains the full BFV key.

cards.title: Why the next resident needs a different writer capability
cards.metric_label: readable dimensions in the proposed bilinear continuation
cards.body: Cross-input interaction could make hidden state affect future answers. In the inspected construction, however, the surviving writer already contains basis encodings. Combined with the output keys, they reveal all 576 variable semantic coordinates. A public span calculation establishes the consequence.
cards.limit: This is a scoped credential and functionality obstruction, not a cryptographic attack execution or an impossibility theorem for private learning. It identifies a design that should change before implementation.

cards.title: The actual polynomial verifier, joined
cards.metric_label: native batching connected to packed commitment extraction
cards.body: The Lean theorem connects the actual batching loop, commitment-time words, folding equations and 38 query positions. A failed common polynomial explanation implies an explicit acceptance bound, with shaped extraction failure kept separate.
cards.limit: Fresh independent challenges and off-domain openings are assumptions. This is the pinned old profile, not the corrected range profile or a deployed security-bit estimate. Application constraints, Fiat–Shamir and arbitrary native refinement remain separate.

cards.title: Certifying a private continuation
cards.metric_label: conditional rooted ancestry from encrypted witnesses
cards.body: A private issuer specializes a public continuation program and certifies its exact parent, child and permitted release. Tagged encrypted witnesses plus simulation-sound proofs give online extraction in the security reduction, including adaptive feedback. The deployed setup retains no witness reader.
cards.limit: A classical conditional construction: general obfuscation, honest setup erasure and a finite horizon remain. Primitive implementations and useful repeated-size bounds are absent; post-quantum certification alone would not make the whole resident post-quantum.

cards.title: Useful features, exact encrypted replay
cards.body: A selected public semantic fixture completed 384 Learn events, 96 Infer events and 256 exact-original expiries through BFV and an independently verifying durable receiver. One shared-machine run took 219.733 seconds.
cards.limit: The receiver retains the full BFV key. This selected subset has 28/32 correct final labels; exact arithmetic does not make every semantic answer correct.

cards.title: A useful, deliberately small semantic learner
cards.body: A frozen SmolLM3 factual scorer feeds a four-bin recency learner. Original features score 51.0010% on the same fresh synthetic text/history study. All eleven preregistered gates passed.
cards.limit: A trusted plaintext issuer supplies the abstraction. The study is local and synthetic, with repeated texts across histories. Spanning exact-score credentials reveal its small aggregate image.

cards.title: A complete designated-recipient workload
cards.body: The original fixed-span workload completed with all 96 integer comparisons passing. Public processing, independent replay and service shutdown precede private decoding. Public work took 11,697.338 seconds (3h 14m 57s).
cards.limit: Classical DDH, a known public fixture, honest setup/erasure and shared-account processes. Recipient credentials still read their full fixed per-input query span outside the journal. Final label accuracy remains 18/32.

cards.title: Public-coin setup joins the durable journal
cards.body: The honest public constructor generates no scalar master. Its journal join completed all 44 independent transition replays; both ordered histories agree and all four private integers match the fixture. Reopening and exact historical retries preserve the head.
cards.limit: Honest sampling and independent recipient registration remain premises. Recipients retain the full per-input fixed span, including expired inputs. The setup proof excludes the instrumented timing view; this arithmetic fixture establishes no model utility or whole-protocol privacy.

cards.title: A complete nonlinear encrypted trajectory
cards.body: The Lean-emitted schedules ran through a generic TFHE interpreter. Every independent-process byte replay matched. After public verification closed, all 484 authorized primary state and sign checks matched the frozen integer fixture.
cards.limit: The full reader key remains. This reused fixture is not a new utility study, universal determinism proof or unrestricted-exposure privacy demonstration. Rust/TFHE and accepted-history release remain separate.

cards.title: A longer replay stops at Learn 14
cards.body: The first thirteen Learn replay pairs match; the fourteenth produces different ciphertext bytes from identical public inputs. A separate emitted runtime with a fixed FFT plan later passes five preregistered replay pairs, including that public input case.
cards.limit: Byte mismatch does not imply incorrect plaintext. The five controls are independent cases, not a completed learning trajectory; no new plaintext decoding was done. They establish neither the old cause nor general deterministic replay.

cards.title: A checked collection of formal ingredients
cards.body: The complete project import closure passed its source build, four umbrellas, patch application and import boundaries. The proposal joins learner arithmetic and emitted schedules with full unique decoding and coherent BabyBear query bounds.
cards.limit: A proposed companion patch. External package/toolchain artifacts were cached; project modules were rebuilt. This does not establish Rust/TFHE refinement, private release or deployed soundness.

cards.title: A security number needs its assumptions
cards.body: The current verdict ledger distinguishes unique-decoding, idealised Johnson and legacy capacity accounting. The withdrawn capacity figure must not be presented as the system’s security level.
cards.limit: This is a guide to the repository’s current verdicts, not a fresh protocol audit. Query accounting and commit-phase error must not silently become a whole-system claim.

cards.title: Private continuation with a fixed horizon
cards.body: Independent functional-encryption instances are set up backwards, so each transition embeds an already existing future public key. The argument retains the whole future key package in the adversary’s view.
cards.limit: A classical, selective-state construction direction under explicit primitive assumptions and honest erasure. Public commands, copying and authorized branches remain. The symbolic witness does not implement encryption.

cards.title: A private resident needs restricted read authority
cards.body: The target releases only the authorized answer while preserving reusable protected state. A journal can regulate a published history; surviving keys may still read inputs or support local counterfactual computations.
cards.limit: Successful encrypted arithmetic, durable integrity and useful adaptation are separate properties. Their current demonstrations do not establish full mental autarky under the declared exposure game.

cards.title: A conditional post-quantum route, with costs
cards.metric_label: finite sizing is not a security level
cards.body: Independent review accepts a conditional fixed-policy LWE construction. A narrower QPT argument permits smaller widths. One n = 1,024 sizing example still needs 84.43 MB per ciphertext and 86.46 GB of public matrices; these are calculated, packed sizes, not generated objects.
cards.limit: The example normalizes unresolved source constants. Gaussian implementation error, reduction errors and computational hardness remain open. Fixed per-input recipient leakage persists, and receipt composition is separate. No whole-resident post-quantum result is claimed.
